title: 5x-review-2: review matching + surfacing channels
description:
## Parent

sutra/150 — Code-anchored lessons: sutra_remember / contextual surfacing

## What to review

All anchor matching mechanisms and surfacing channels are active. Lessons match by symbol, file glob, import pattern, and directory glob. All three tools (sutra_read, sutra_impact, sutra_orient) surface matching lessons. FTS5 explicit queries work via sutra_lessons. Category filtering prevents cross-language noise.

**Reviewer focus:**
- Matching correctness — are the glob/import/directory patterns matching the right things and not matching the wrong things?
- Surfacing format consistency — do lessons look the same across read/impact/orient responses?
- Category inference and filtering logic — is the workspace language/tech profile used correctly?
- FTS5 query ergonomics — are the results useful for agents?
- Volume — with all matching active, are there scenarios where too many lessons surface?

**vidhi-sutra-tend moment:** Matching engine structure has settled. Good time to lock down anchor kind vocabulary, matching conventions, and the MatchContext interface before the lifecycle/enrichment slices build on them.

## Blocked by

- sutra/153 — File glob + import pattern + directory anchor matching
- sutra/154 — FTS5 + sutra_lessons query tool
- sutra/155 — Categories + cross-project filtering
- sutra/156 — sutra_impact + sutra_orient lesson injection

messages.author: codex
messages.text:
Codex adversarial review: 5 findings (3 high, 2 medium). All fixed in a9f2021.

1. [HIGH] Language-tag bypass in category filtering — mixed lang+tech categories leaked cross-language
2. [HIGH] Project scoping None in impact/orient — cross-project lesson leakage
3. [HIGH] No surfacing cap — unbounded results from broad anchors
4. [MED] File glob * crosses dir separators — false positives on nested paths
5. [MED] FTS5 raw syntax exposure — punctuation/operators in agent queries"
